title: Bicycle Sports in Beaumont to close next month - NewsBreak
text:
By Mbu Maqungo ,
7 hours ago The home of Bicycle Sports in Beaumont, Texas on Sept 23, 2025. (Mbu Maqungo/For The Beaumont Enterprise) One of Beaumont's featured bike shops will soon close its doors after decades of service.
Bicycle Sports plans to close permanently Oct. 18, according to owner Eric Bender.
Offering a range of bikes, electric models and repair services at various places around town since 1984, Bender saw multiple generations of Southeast Texans develop a love for cycling from his spot at 2770 I-10 Interstate 10.
“There are plans for a party or celebration to close things out,” Bender said. “We’re in the process of closing, unless someone steps up that’s interested in purchasing a smaller fixture for the business, or just transitioning into a service center.”
According to Bender, e-commerce has taken at least 40% off the top of his gross volume, in addition to consumer habits shifting towards direct purchases from vendors.
RELATED: The catch-up on the most recent Business roundup
Bender said that his decades of experience and familiarity in the community were some of the factors that helped solve specific customer issues and keep the business afloat during tumultuous times, but changes in the business model and cost of maintaining an inventory of bikes and e-bikes made the current operation untenable.
“It’s hard to live on the $80 when the $600 is going somewhere else,” he said. “I’m getting too old to fight these battles, so before a bank comes in and closes us, we decided to shut it down. I’ve given up on putting price tags on merchandise. We are having arbitrary inflation under the tariffs, but we had inflation before. So did the tariffs hurt us? Yes. Were we already hurting? Yes.”
RELATED: 12 students hospitalized after odor reported at Beaumont middle school
Bender recalled a customer who called the previous weekend looking for a specific length and size of seat post.
“Although I didn’t have exactly what they asked for, I knew I had tricks of the trade and manufactured items to solve their problem,” he described. “It’s not an obvious solution, and I’m not hiding anything. It’s all above the table.”
Bender expressed a deep gratitude for the decades of service he was able to provide for local cyclists. He said this won’t change him, and he will still be around town riding his bike.
